name: App
first: The type that a SwiftUI app starts from, whose body lists the app's scenes.

dependsOn.why: An app's body lists its scenes.
An app is usually a structure.
An app is a type that conforms to SwiftUI's app protocol.
The type of an app's body is an opaque type that names the scene protocol.

what.is: An app is a type that conforms to the protocol `App`. Its `body` lists the scenes that the app has, such as a window group. In an app, it is the type that the app starts from.
what.afterExample: `TripsApp` has one scene, a window group that shows a `Text`. Line 12 reads its `body`, as SwiftUI does when the app starts, and prints {{WindowGroup<Text>}}.
what.problem: Every app needs a place to start, and a list of what it shows. In UIKit, an app delegate and a scene delegate made the windows in code. In SwiftUI, an app is a type whose `body` lists its scenes, and SwiftUI makes them.
what.how: The protocol `App` gives each app a static method that starts the app. When the app starts, SwiftUI makes an instance of the app's type, reads its `body`, and makes its scenes, which show their views.

when.text: Use it once in each app, with the attribute `@main` before it. `@main` marks the type that the app starts from, and the system then calls the static method that `App` gives it, which starts the app:
Don't put the app's screens in it. Its `body` lists scenes, and each scene shows a view, which is where the screens are.
